implementation_notes: Rails already ships the pattern: every controller inherits ApplicationController, and before_action callbacks declared there run the shared security sequence before any action, delegating authentication to Warden/Devise and authorization to a policy layer such as Pundit. The base controller takes the role of the secure base action, and subclasses add callbacks or opt out with skip_before_action where a public action is intended. Site-wide concerns that must run above the router are handled by Rack middleware instead.
code_sketch:
class ApplicationController < ActionController::Base
  before_action :authenticate_user!          # Devise (Warden)
  before_action :verify_session
  after_action  :audit_action

  def verify_session
    redirect_to(new_user_session_path) unless session_valid?(session)
  end
end
pitfalls: Declaring the callbacks in ApplicationController does not cover controllers inheriting from ActionController::API or those that skip them; audit exemptions explicitly.
A before_action that renders or redirects halts the chain, so nothing else runs - including the intended audit.
Callbacks are inherited in declaration order and can be re-ordered per controller; keep the security callbacks together and pin the order in tests.
